The specs don't yet mark deprecations with `deprecated: true`, and the API sends no `Deprecation` or `Sunset` headers. Read the changelog and the field descriptions instead.

## Recommendations for integrators and agents

- Use `/v2` for anything that moves money or feeds production decisions.
- If you depend on beta or alpha, pin the fields you read, validate responses at runtime, and alert on schema drift.
- Ignore unknown response fields. Don't use strict "no additional properties" validation on responses. The rewards-context response already returns fewer network keys than the spec marks as required.
- Never hard-code the network list. Read it from `GET /v2/networks`.
- Re-check the defaults described on [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions#defaults-per-endpoint) when you upgrade, and pass important filters (`allowedNetworks`, `minTvl`, `sortOrder`) explicitly instead of relying on defaults.

Not in this condensed core (What may change, by level; How to detect changes): see https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/versioning.md.


# Recipes: executed end-to-end examples for the vaults.fyi API
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/overview

> Index of tested vaults.fyi recipes (ranking, pagination, APY display, history vs benchmark, positions, deposits, withdrawals, rewards, errors, credits, identifiers, attribution, Solana), each mapped to the task it solves.

This page lists the vaults.fyi recipes: complete, runnable examples that solve one integration task end to end, each in curl, Python and TypeScript. Pick the recipe that matches your task; each page stands alone with prerequisites, credit cost, steps, real output and pitfalls.

Every snippet on these pages was executed against the live API on 2026-10-23, read-only, with the public address `0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045`. Transaction recipes build and verify unsigned payloads and show how to sign with viem; **no transaction was signed or broadcast**. All REST calls use `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`.

## Tasks not covered by a recipe

These benchmark tasks are answered by reference pages rather than code recipes:

| Task | Where |
| - | - |
| T06: connect the MCP server to Claude Code | [MCP server](/ai-agents/mcp-server) |
| T08: keyless x402 call and its price | [x402](/ai-agents/x402) |
| T11: idle tokens → deposit options | [Portfolio tracking](/concepts/portfolio-tracking) |
| T22: what to verify before signing (also in the deposit recipe) | [Transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety) |
| T23: is beta/alpha production-safe? | [Versioning](/api-reference/versioning) |
| T25: which MCP tool and arguments for a filtered search | [MCP server](/ai-agents/mcp-server) |

## Rules every recipe follows

- **Auth:** `x-api-key` header on REST. Without it, v2 endpoints return 402 (x402 payment challenge), not 401.
- **Units:** APY is a decimal fraction, net of fees. Token amounts are base-unit integer strings. Timestamps are Unix seconds.
- **Defaults:** list and portfolio endpoints search only base, mainnet, arbitrum and optimism unless you pass `allowedNetworks`; `/v2/detailed-vaults` also defaults to `minTvl=100000` and `sortOrder=asc`.
- **Arrays:** repeat the query key (`allowedNetworks=base&allowedNetworks=arbitrum`).
- **Pagination:** `nextPage` is absent on the last page.
- **Soft errors:** a 200 can carry `errors.unsupported*`; treat non-empty lists as errors.
- **Transactions:** context first, verify every action, send in order, never let an API or agent hold a private key.


# Recipe: find and rank vaults (top USDC vaults by 7-day APY)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/find-and-rank-vaults

> Executed recipe: query GET /v2/detailed-vaults for the top USDC vaults on chosen networks by 7-day APY with a TVL floor, no warnings and a minimum Reputation Score, in curl, Python, TypeScript and both SDKs.

This recipe answers "which vaults should I show for asset X on network Y, ranked by yield?" It returns the top 5 USDC vaults on Base and Arbitrum by 7-day APY with at least $10M TVL and no warnings, then narrows to established vaults by Reputation Score. Use it for an Earn screen, an allowlist, or an agent answering "best USDC yield on Base".

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. APY values are decimal fractions (`0.0578` = 5.78 %), already net of fees. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real and trimmed.

## Credit cost

`GET /v2/detailed-vaults` costs **1 credit per call + 3 per vault returned** ([credits](/plans/credits)). With `perPage=5` and 5 results: 1 + 5 × 3 = **16 credits**. The established-vault query below (`perPage=3`) costs 10. Keep `perPage` small: every returned vault costs 3.

## Step 1: rank by 7-day APY with a TVL floor

The query needs five non-default settings:

| Parameter | Value | Why |
| - | - | - |
| `allowedNetworks` | `base`, `arbitrum` (repeat the key) | Default is 4 networks: base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism. A comma list (`base,arbitrum`) is treated as one unknown network. |
| `minTvl` | `10000000` | Integer USD. Default is `100000`. |
| `sortBy` / `sortOrder` | `apy7day` / `desc` | `sortOrder` defaults to `asc`, which returns the **lowest** APYs first. `sortBy=apy` is a 400; valid values are `tvl`, `apy1day`, `apy7day`, `apy30day`, `apy90day`. |
| `allowVaultsWithWarnings` | `false` | Defaults to `true` on this endpoint. |
| `onlyTransactional` | `true` | Only vaults the Transactions API can build deposits for. Drop it for data-only screens. |

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/find-and-rank-vaults.md

### Python

```python
"""Top 5 USDC vaults on Base + Arbitrum by 7-day APY, TVL >= $10M, no warnings."""
import os

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}

params = [  # list of tuples -> repeated keys for array params
    ("allowedAssets", "USDC"),
    ("allowedNetworks", "base"),
    ("allowedNetworks", "arbitrum"),
    ("minTvl", 10_000_000),          # integer USD (default is 100000)
    ("allowVaultsWithWarnings", "false"),  # default is true on this endpoint
    ("onlyTransactional", "true"),
    ("sortBy", "apy7day"),
    ("sortOrder", "desc"),           # default is asc -> lowest APY first
    ("perPage", 5),
]
r = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/detailed-vaults", headers=HEADERS, params=params, timeout=30)
r.raise_for_status()
body = r.json()

# Soft errors: unknown filter values return 200 + errors.unsupported*, not 400.
bad = {k: v for k, v in (body.get("errors") or {}).items() if v}
if bad:
    raise SystemExit(f"Filter values were rejected: {bad}")

for v in body["data"]:
    apy7 = v["apy"]["7day"]["total"]  # decimal fraction: 0.0412 means 4.12 %
    print(f'{v["network"]["name"]:9} {v["name"][:40]:40} '
          f'7d APY {apy7 * 100:6.2f} %  TVL ${int(v["tvl"]["usd"]):>13,}  '
          f'score {v["score"]["vaultScore"]:.1f}  vaultId {v["vaultId"]}')
print("itemsOnPage:", body["itemsOnPage"], "| nextPage:", body.get("nextPage", "absent (last page)"))
```

### TypeScript

`nextPage: 1` means more results exist; it is absent on the last page. `errors.unsupported*` lists filter values the API did not recognise; the snippets stop if any are non-empty, because the API answers 200 with fewer (or zero) results instead of a 400.

## Step 2: only established vaults

To keep only vaults with a track record, add `minVaultScore` (Reputation Score, 0 to 100; observed 27.5–99.1) and exclude warnings. Corrupted data is already excluded: `allowCorrupted` defaults to `false`. If you need a strict threshold, check `score.vaultScore`, `warnings[]` and `isCorrupted` on each result client-side before you show it.

The score threshold is a product decision; 70 is an example, not a vaults.fyi recommendation. See [Reputation Score](/methodology/reputation-score) for what the score measures.

## The same query with the SDKs

The SDKs send array parameters as repeated keys and return the same envelope `{ itemsOnPage, nextPage?, data, errors }`; the result is **not** an array.

Python, `vaultsfyi` 1.3.0:

```python
"""Same query with the published Python SDK (vaultsfyi 1.3.0)."""
import os

from vaultsfyi import VaultsSdk

client = VaultsSdk(api_key=os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"])

page = client.get_detailed_vaults(  # get_all_vaults is a deprecated alias
    allowed_assets=["USDC"],
    allowed_networks=["base", "arbitrum"],  # sent as repeated keys
    min_tvl=10_000_000,
    allow_vaults_with_warnings=False,
    only_transactional=True,
    sort_by="apy7day",
    sort_order="desc",
    per_page=5,
)
for v in page["data"]:
    print(v["network"]["name"], v["name"], f'{v["apy"]["7day"]["total"] * 100:.2f} %', v["vaultId"])
```

Both printed the same five vaults as the REST call above.

## Pitfalls

- **Missing `sortOrder=desc`.** The default is ascending: you get the worst yields.
- **Comma-joined arrays.** `allowedNetworks=base,arbitrum` returns 200, `itemsOnPage: 0` and `errors.unsupportedNetworks: ["base,arbitrum"]`. Repeat the key.
- **Default network scope.** Without `allowedNetworks`, only base, mainnet, arbitrum and optimism are searched.
- **`minTvl` units.** Integer USD (`10000000` for $10M), not millions, not a float.
- **APY display.** Multiply by 100 for percent. Don't subtract fees: APY is already net. Values are not clamped: on 2026-10-23 a small Base vault reported a 7-day APY of 152,563 %; filter by `minTvl` and score before showing them.
- **`/v2/vaults` is not for ranking.** It returns identity fields only (no APY or TVL).
- **Trusting `minVaultScore` alone.** Check `score.vaultScore` client-side if you need a strict threshold ([Reputation Score](/methodology/reputation-score)).
- **`network=8453` or `network=ethereum`** are rejected; use `base` / `mainnet` or CAIP-2 (`eip155:8453`). See [network and vault IDs](/recipes/network-and-vault-ids).


# Recipe: paginate every vault (stop when nextPage is absent)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/paginate-all-vaults

> Executed recipe: fetch every page of a vaults.fyi list endpoint, stop when nextPage is absent, override the 4-network and minTvl defaults, and budget credits, in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "how do I get **all** vaults, not just the first page?" It pages through `/v2/vaults` (identity list, every network) and `/v2/detailed-vaults` (full metrics) until the last page, overrides the defaults that silently hide vaults, and estimates the credit cost. Use it for bulk exports, nightly syncs and analytics backfills.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real and trimmed.

## How pagination works

| Rule | Value |
| - | - |
| Envelope | `{ itemsOnPage, nextPage?, data: [...], errors? }` |
| First page | `page=0` (zero-based) |
| Last page | `nextPage` is **absent** (the key is missing, it is never `null`) |
| Page size | `perPage` default 50, max 5000 (historical endpoints: 20000); `0` is a 400 |
| Total count | Not returned. Count rows yourself. |
| Unpaginated | `/v2/portfolio/*` returns `{ data, errors }` with no `nextPage` |

## Credit cost

| Endpoint | Cost | This run |
| - | - | - |
| `GET /v2/vaults` | 1 per call, any `perPage` | 3,662 vaults in 1 call (`perPage=5000`) = **1 credit** |
| `GET /v2/detailed-vaults` | 1 per call + 3 per vault returned | 72 USDT0 vaults in 8 pages = 8 + 216 = **224 credits** |

A full-market `/v2/detailed-vaults` pull costs about 3 credits per vault, so 3,662 vaults ≈ 11,000 credits. Pull identities from `/v2/vaults` and fetch detail only for the vaults you need ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## Step 1: the loop (curl)

This loop pages USDT0 vaults on Plasma and Ethereum with `perPage=10` to show several pages; use a larger `perPage` in production.

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/paginate-all-vaults.md

## Step 2: a reusable fetch-all (Python)

```python
"""Fetch every page of a vaults.fyi list endpoint safely (stop when nextPage is absent)."""
import os
import time

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
session = requests.Session()
session.headers["x-api-key"] = os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]


def fetch_all(path, params, per_page=1000, max_pages=1000):
    """Return (rows, calls). params is a list of (key, value) tuples so array
    params can repeat. page is zero-based; nextPage is OMITTED on the last page."""
    rows, page, calls = [], 0, 0
    while calls < max_pages:  # hard cap: never loop forever
        r = session.get(f"{API}{path}", params=params + [("page", page), ("perPage", per_page)], timeout=60)
        r.raise_for_status()
        body = r.json()
        calls += 1
        bad = {k: v for k, v in (body.get("errors") or {}).items() if v}
        if bad:
            raise ValueError(f"filter values rejected: {bad}")
        rows.extend(body["data"])
        if "nextPage" not in body:  # last page: key absent (never null)
            break
        page = body["nextPage"]
        time.sleep(0.2)  # stay well under your plan's rate limit
    return rows, calls


# 1) Identity list of every NON-CORRUPTED vault on every network: /v2/vaults has no default
#    network filter and costs a flat 1 credit per call.
vaults, calls = fetch_all("/v2/vaults", [], per_page=5000)
networks = sorted({v["network"]["name"] for v in vaults})
print(f"/v2/vaults: {len(vaults)} vaults on {len(networks)} networks in {calls} call(s)")

# 2) Detailed data across ALL networks. /v2/detailed-vaults defaults to
#    base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism and minTvl=100000 -- override both.
#    These recorded queries exclude corrupted vaults; see the full-inventory flags above.
#    Take network names from the vault list: /v2/networks also lists networks
#    with no vaults, which detailed-vaults reports in errors.unsupportedNetworks.
params = [("allowedNetworks", n) for n in networks] + [("allowedAssets", "USDT0"), ("minTvl", 0)]
detailed, calls = fetch_all("/v2/detailed-vaults", params, per_page=10)
credits = calls * 1 + 3 * len(detailed)  # 1 credit per call + 3 per vault returned
print(f"/v2/detailed-vaults USDT0: {len(detailed)} vaults in {calls} pages, ~{credits} credits")
for v in sorted(detailed, key=lambda v: -int(v["tvl"]["usd"]))[:3]:
    print(f'  {v["network"]["name"]:8} {v["name"][:36]:36} TVL ${int(v["tvl"]["usd"]):,}')
```

## Step 2: a reusable fetch-all (TypeScript)

`/v2/vaults` returned 3,662 vaults on 21 networks (22 networks exist; one had no vaults). The detailed query across all 21 networks found 72 USDT0 vaults with `minTvl=0`.

## Pitfalls

- **Checking `nextPage === null` or `nextPage == None`.** It is never null: the key is missing on the last page. Test for presence (`"nextPage" not in body`, `body.nextPage === undefined`).
- **Treating the response as an array.** Rows are in `data`; `itemsOnPage` is the count on this page, not the total.
- **Default scope on `/v2/detailed-vaults`.** Only base, mainnet, arbitrum and optimism, and only vaults with TVL ≥ $100,000. Pass every network (repeated `allowedNetworks` keys), `minTvl=0`, `allowCorrupted=true` and `allowVaultsWithWarnings=true`, with no asset restriction, for a full detailed pull. `/v2/vaults` has no network default but also needs `allowCorrupted=true` for a complete identity list.
- **Taking network names from `/v2/networks`.** It lists networks with no vaults, which `/v2/detailed-vaults` reports in `errors.unsupportedNetworks`; the snippets treat that as an error. Use the names seen in `/v2/vaults`.
- **Unbounded loops.** Cap the number of pages and sleep between calls; watch `x-ratelimit-remaining` ([errors](/api-reference/errors#429-rate-limit-exceeded)).
- **Large `perPage` on detailed endpoints.** Cost scales with rows returned, not calls.


# Recipe: read and display APY correctly (total, base, reward, apyComposite)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/display-apy-correctly

> Executed recipe: read apy.<window>.{base,reward,total} as decimal fractions, pick a window, handle outliers, and use apyComposite on nested vaults, in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "which APY number do I show, and how do I format it?" It reads every APY window of a vault, explains `total` vs `base` vs `reward`, and shows how `apyComposite` changes the answer for nested vaults (vaults whose deposit asset is another vault's share). Use it whenever you render a yield.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. APY values are **decimal fractions** (`0.0315` = 3.15 %), already **net of fees**. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real and trimmed.

## Credit cost

`GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}` costs **3 credits**. If you only need APY, `GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}/apy` costs 1 credit but has no `1hour` window and no `apyComposite` ([credits](/plans/credits)). The Python and TypeScript examples read two vaults: 6 credits.

## The APY fields

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `apy.<window>.base` | Yield from the vault's own strategy (share-price growth), decimal fraction |
| `apy.<window>.reward` | Yield from incentive tokens, decimal fraction |
| `apy.<window>.total` | `base + reward`. Show this one. |
| `<window>` | `1hour`, `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` on detailed-vault responses |
| `rewards[].apy.<window>` | Per-token breakdown of `reward`. Already included in `reward`; don't add it again. |
| `apyComposite` | Only on nested vaults. `intrinsicApy` = the underlying vault's yield; `totalApy` = this vault compounded with it. |

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/display-apy-correctly.md

## Python

```python
"""Read and display a vault's APY correctly (decimal fractions, already net of fees)."""
import os

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}
WINDOWS = ["1hour", "1day", "7day", "30day", "90day"]  # detailed-vault windows


def pct(x):
    """APY fields are decimal fractions: 0.0316 -> '3.16 %'. Never subtract fees."""
    return f"{x * 100:.2f} %"


def show(network, vault_id):
    r = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vault_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30)
    r.raise_for_status()
    v = r.json()
    print(f'{v["name"]} ({network}) asset={v["asset"]["symbol"]}')
    for w in WINDOWS:
        a = v["apy"].get(w)
        if a:
            print(f"  {w:>5}: total {pct(a['total']):>9} = base {pct(a['base'])} + reward {pct(a['reward'])}")
    headline = v["apy"]["7day"]["total"]
    if abs(headline) > 1:  # >100 % / year: unclamped outlier, show with a warning
        print("  WARNING: APY outlier, review before showing to users")
    # rewards[] itemises apy.<window>.reward per token -- it is already included in reward.
    for rw in v.get("rewards", []):
        print(f'  reward token {rw["asset"]["symbol"]}: 7d {pct(rw["apy"]["7day"])} (included in reward)')
    # apyComposite appears only when the vault's asset is itself another vault's share.
    if "apyComposite" in v:
        comp = v["apyComposite"]
        print(f'  apyComposite.totalApy.7day.total    {pct(comp["totalApy"]["7day"]["total"])} (both layers)')
        print(f'  apyComposite.intrinsicApy.7day.total {pct(comp["intrinsicApy"]["7day"]["total"])} (underlying vault)')
    print(f"  -> show users: 7-day total APY {pct(headline)} (net of fees)\n")


show("base", "0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845")      # Steakhouse High Yield USDC
show("mainnet", "0x4Be55238515377Be8b7f167E226bd37a2eB09BCe")   # nested vault with apyComposite
```

## TypeScript

The second vault ("Covered Steakhouse High Yield Instant") accepts another vault's share token (bbqUSDC). Its own `apy.7day.total` is **−1.38 %**, but a depositor earns **4.29 %** in terms of the underlying asset (`apyComposite.totalApy`), because the underlying vault yields 5.75 % (`apyComposite.intrinsicApy`). For nested vaults, decide which one your UI means and label it.

## Pitfalls

- **Showing `0.0315` as "0.03 %".** Multiply by 100.
- **Subtracting fees.** APY is already net of fees.
- **Adding `rewards[]` to `reward`.** It is a breakdown of `reward`, not extra yield.
- **Mixing windows.** Compare vaults on the same window (for example `7day`). `1hour` is noisy.
- **Assuming APY ≥ 0 or ≤ 1.** Values are not clamped; negative values and values above 1 (100 %) occur. Flag outliers.
- **Reading `apyComposite` unconditionally.** The key is absent on non-nested vaults.
- **Flat names from older docs** (`baseApy`, `rewardApy`, `apy7d`) do not exist in responses.


# Recipe: 90 days of daily APY and comparison with the USD benchmark
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/vault-history-vs-benchmark

> Executed recipe: fetch daily 7-day APY for the last 90 days with granularity=1day and Unix-second timestamps, then compare a vault with the network's USD benchmark (code=usd), in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "how has this vault's yield moved over the last 90 days, and is it beating the market?" It pulls one daily 7-day-APY point per day from the historical API, then compares the vault's current 7-day APY with the network's USD benchmark on the same window. Use it for charts, allocator reports and "above/below market" badges.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. APY values are decimal fractions; timestamps are **Unix seconds**. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real and trimmed.

## Credit cost

| Call | Cost | This run |
| - | - | - |
| `GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/apy` | 1 per call + 1 per point | 90 points = **91 credits** |
| `GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}` | 3 | 3 |
| `GET /v2/benchmarks/{network}?code=usd` | 3 | 3 |

The combined endpoint `/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}` (APY + TVL + share price) costs 3 + 3 per point: 273 credits for the same 90 days ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## Parameters that matter

| Parameter | Value here | Default | Note |
| - | - | - | - |
| `granularity` | `1day` | `1hour` | Spacing of points: `1hour`, `1day`, `1week`. |
| `apyInterval` | `7day` | `7day` | Smoothing window of each point: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day`. Not the same as `granularity`. |
| `fromTimestamp` / `toTimestamp` | now − 90 days / now | — | Unix **seconds**. Milliseconds are a 400. |
| `perPage` | `100` | `50` | With the defaults you get 50 hourly points (about 2 days). |
| `code` (benchmarks) | `usd` | required | `usd` or `eth`. Missing → 400. |

## curl

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/vault-history-vs-benchmark.md

Points are oldest first. In this response `nextPage` is `null` because the jq filter reads a key that is absent; the API itself omitted `nextPage` (last page).

## Python

```python
"""90 days of daily APY for one vault, compared with the network's USD benchmark."""
import os
import time

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}
NETWORK, VAULT_ID = "base", "0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845"  # Steakhouse High Yield USDC

to_ts = int(time.time()) // 86400 * 86400  # Unix SECONDS (milliseconds -> 400)
from_ts = to_ts - 90 * 86400

# 1) History. granularity defaults to 1hour and perPage to 50: set both or you get 50 hourly points.
points, page = [], 0
while True:
    r = requests.get(
        f"{API}/v2/historical/{NETWORK}/{VAULT_ID}/apy",
        headers=HEADERS,
        params={"granularity": "1day", "apyInterval": "7day", "fromTimestamp": from_ts,
                "toTimestamp": to_ts, "perPage": 100, "page": page},
        timeout=30,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    body = r.json()
    points += body["data"]  # oldest first
    if "nextPage" not in body:
        break
    page = body["nextPage"]
print(f"{len(points)} daily points, cost ~{1 + len(points)} credits (1 per call + 1 per point)")
print("first", time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.gmtime(points[0]["timestamp"])), f'{points[0]["apy"]["total"] * 100:.2f} %')
print("last ", time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.gmtime(points[-1]["timestamp"])), f'{points[-1]["apy"]["total"] * 100:.2f} %')

# 2) Current vault APY and the benchmark, SAME window (7day). code is required: usd or eth.
vault = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/detailed-vaults/{NETWORK}/{VAULT_ID}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30).json()
bench = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/benchmarks/{NETWORK}", headers=HEADERS, params={"code": "usd"}, timeout=30).json()
v7, b7 = vault["apy"]["7day"]["total"], bench["apy"]["7day"]["total"]
spread_bp = round((v7 - b7) * 10_000)  # decimal fractions -> basis points
print(f"vault 7d {v7 * 100:.2f} % vs USD benchmark 7d {b7 * 100:.2f} % -> {spread_bp:+d} bp "
      f'({"beating" if v7 > b7 else "below"} benchmark)')
```

## Historical benchmarks

`GET /v2/historical-benchmarks/{network}?code=usd` returns the benchmark over time (3 credits + 3 per point). Benchmarks are computed once per UTC day.

## Pitfalls

- **Default `granularity=1hour` with default `perPage=50`.** You silently get 50 hourly points, not 90 days.
- **Millisecond timestamps** (`Date.now()`): 400. Divide by 1000.
- **Confusing `apyInterval` with `granularity`.** One is the smoothing window, the other the spacing.
- **Comparing different windows.** Compare the vault's `apy.7day.total` with the benchmark's `apy.7day.total`.
- **Calling benchmarks without `code`.** It is required; it selects one benchmark (`usd` or `eth`).
- **Reading `nextPage` as null.** It is absent on the last page.


# Recipe: wallet positions with correct balance math
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/positions-and-balances

> Executed recipe: list a wallet's vault positions with GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}, convert asset.positionValueInAsset from base units, and avoid counting asset.balanceNative (the idle wallet balance), in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "how much does this wallet hold in each vault, in human units and USD?" It lists all positions on the chosen networks and converts each position size correctly. Use it for portfolio screens and for agents asked "what is my balance in vault X?"

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Amounts are **base-unit integer strings**. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23 against the public address `0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045`; outputs are real and trimmed.

## Credit cost

`GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}` costs **5 credits** per call, whatever it returns. One vault: `GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` costs 1 ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## Which field is the position

| Field | Meaning | Unit |
| - | - | - |
| `asset.positionValueInAsset` | **The position**, valued in the deposit asset | asset base units (÷ 10^`asset.decimals`) |
| `lpToken.balanceNative` | Vault shares held | share base units (÷ 10^`lpToken.decimals`) |
| `lpToken.balanceUsd` | The position in USD (may be absent) | USD decimal string |
| `asset.balanceNative` / `asset.balanceUsd` | The wallet's **idle** balance of the deposit asset, outside the vault | base units / USD |

Adding `asset.balanceNative` to the position double-counts: it is the same idle balance repeated on every position with that asset.

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/positions-and-balances.md

## Python

```python
"""List a wallet's vault positions with correct balance math (base units, no double counting)."""
import os
from decimal import Decimal

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}
USER = "0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045"
NETWORKS = ["base", "mainnet", "arbitrum", "optimism"]  # default scope; add more to see other chains

r = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/portfolio/positions/{USER}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30,
                 params=[("allowedNetworks", n) for n in NETWORKS])
r.raise_for_status()
body = r.json()  # {"data": [...], "errors": {...}} -- not paginated, no nextPage


def tokens(raw, decimals):
    """Base-unit integer string -> Decimal tokens. Never use float for amounts."""
    return Decimal(raw) / (Decimal(10) ** decimals)


total_usd = Decimal(0)
for p in body["data"]:
    a = p["asset"]
    size = tokens(a["positionValueInAsset"], a["decimals"])  # the position, in asset units
    usd = Decimal(p["lpToken"].get("balanceUsd") or 0)          # the position, in USD (may be absent)
    total_usd += usd
    idle = tokens(a["balanceNative"], a["decimals"])           # wallet's IDLE balance of the asset
    print(f'{p["network"]["name"]:8} {p["name"][:30]:30} position {size:.6f} {a["symbol"]} (~${usd:,.2f})'
          f'   [idle {a["symbol"]} in wallet: {idle:.4f} -- do not add]')
print(f"{len(body['data'])} positions, total ~${total_usd:,.2f} (sum of lpToken.balanceUsd)")
```

## TypeScript

Note how the same idle ETH balance (5.7733) appears on every ETH-denominated position: it is the wallet balance, not part of the positions.

## Pitfalls

- **Using `asset.balanceNative` as the position size.** It is the wallet's idle balance. Use `asset.positionValueInAsset`.
- **Float math on base units.** 18-decimal amounts overflow float precision; use `Decimal` or `BigInt`.
- **Share vs asset units.** `lpToken.balanceNative` is in shares; shares and assets differ unless the share price is 1.
- **Expecting pagination.** `/v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}` returns `{ data, errors }`, no `nextPage`.
- **Default 4-network scope.** Positions on other networks are not returned unless you pass them in `allowedNetworks`.
- **Returns and events** (`/v2/portfolio/total-returns/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`, `/v2/portfolio/events/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`) are only meaningful when the vault has `userEventsIndexed: true`.


# Recipe: build, verify and sign a vault deposit (EVM)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/deposit-transaction

> Executed recipe: read GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}, build GET /v2/transactions/deposit/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId} with assetAddress and a base-unit amount, decode and verify every action, then sign in order with viem (shown, not executed), in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "how do I deposit N tokens into a vault for a user?" It reads the transaction context, builds the unsigned payload for a base-unit amount, verifies chain, target, value and decoded arguments of every action, and shows how to sign them in order with viem. Use it in wallets, apps and agents that execute deposits. vaults.fyi never signs or holds funds: your wallet signs.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. `amount` is a **base-unit integer string** (1,000 USDC = `1000000000`; 25 USDC = `25000000`). All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23 against the public address `0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045`; outputs are real and trimmed. **The signing step was not executed**: the tests run without `SEND=1`.

## Credit cost

| Call | Cost |
| - | - |
| `GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | 3 |
| `GET /v2/transactions/deposit/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | 5 |
| **One deposit flow** | **8 credits** |

([credits](/plans/credits)). Path order is **user, network, vault**.

## Step 1: context, then payload (curl)

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/deposit-transaction.md

`currentDepositStep: "deposit"` means the vault accepts a direct deposit now. `actions` must be sent in order, from `currentActionIndex`: the approval, then the deposit. The live payload has **no `value` key** on these ERC-20 actions (jq prints the missing key as `null`): treat a missing `value` as 0, as the snippets do (`BigInt(value ?? 0)`).

## Step 2: verify every action (Python)

The Python example builds and verifies only; sign with your wallet library.

## Step 3: verify and sign in order (TypeScript, viem)

The signing branch runs only when `SEND=1` and `PRIVATE_KEY` are set. Keep keys in the user's wallet; never send them to any API.

```typescript
// Build, verify and (only when SEND=1) sign a deposit with viem. Tests never set SEND.
import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http, decodeFunctionData, erc20Abi, erc4626Abi, getAddress, type Hex } from 'viem';
import { privateKeyToAccount } from 'viem/accounts';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';

const API = 'https://api.vaults.fyi';
const headers = { 'x-api-key': process.env.VAULTSFYI_API_KEY! };
const USER = getAddress('0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045');
const NETWORK = 'base';
const VAULT_ID = getAddress('0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845'); // Steakhouse High Yield USDC
const HUMAN_AMOUNT = '25'; // 25 USDC

async function get(path: string, params: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const qs = new URLSearchParams(params);
  const res = await fetch(`${API}${path}${qs.size ? `?${qs}` : ''}`, { headers });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
  return res.json();
}

// 1) Context: next step, asset address/decimals, wallet balance.
const ctx = await get(`/v2/transactions/context/${USER}/${NETWORK}/${VAULT_ID}`);
if (ctx.currentDepositStep !== 'deposit') throw new Error(`next step is ${ctx.currentDepositStep}`);
const asset = ctx.asset as { address: Hex; symbol: string; decimals: number; balanceNative: string };
const [whole, frac = ''] = HUMAN_AMOUNT.split('.');
const amount = BigInt(whole + frac.padEnd(asset.decimals, '0').slice(0, asset.decimals)); // exact base units
if (amount > BigInt(asset.balanceNative)) throw new Error(`insufficient ${asset.symbol}`); // API doesn't check

// 2) Payload: assetAddress required, amount as base-unit string.
const payload = await get(`/v2/transactions/deposit/${USER}/${NETWORK}/${VAULT_ID}`, {
  assetAddress: asset.address,
  amount: amount.toString(),
});

// 3) Verify chain, target and decoded arguments of every action.
type Action = { name: string; tx: { to: Hex; chainId: number; data?: Hex; value?: string } };
const actions: Action[] = payload.actions;
for (const [i, a] of actions.entries()) {
  const { to, chainId, data, value } = a.tx;
  if (chainId !== base.id) throw new Error(`action ${i}: wrong chain ${chainId}`);
  if (![getAddress(asset.address), VAULT_ID].includes(getAddress(to))) throw new Error(`action ${i}: unexpected target ${to}`);
  if (BigInt(value ?? 0) !== 0n) throw new Error(`action ${i}: unexpected native value`);
  if (getAddress(to) === getAddress(asset.address)) {
    const { functionName, args } = decodeFunctionData({ abi: erc20Abi, data });
    if (functionName !== 'approve' || getAddress(args[0] as Hex) !== VAULT_ID || args[1] !== amount)
      throw new Error(`action ${i}: approval is not exactly ${amount} to the vault`);
  } else {
    const { functionName, args } = decodeFunctionData({ abi: erc4626Abi, data });
    if (functionName !== 'deposit' || args[0] !== amount || getAddress(args[1] as Hex) !== USER)
      throw new Error(`action ${i}: deposit args mismatch`);
  }
  console.log(`action ${i}: ${a.name}  to=${to}  OK`);
}
console.log(`verified ${actions.length} actions for ${HUMAN_AMOUNT} ${asset.symbol} (${amount} base units)`);

// 4) Sign and send IN ORDER, waiting for each receipt. Gated: never runs unless SEND=1.
if (process.env.SEND === '1') {
  const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PRIVATE_KEY as Hex); // must be USER's key; never hard-code it
  const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: base, transport: http() });
  const pub = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
  for (const a of actions.slice(payload.currentActionIndex)) {
    const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({ to: a.tx.to, ...(a.tx.data !== undefined ? { data: a.tx.data } : {}), value: BigInt(a.tx.value ?? 0) });
    const receipt = await pub.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });
    if (receipt.status !== 'success') throw new Error(`${a.name} reverted: ${hash}`);
    console.log(`${a.name}: ${hash}`);
  }
} else {
  console.log('SEND!=1: not signing (dry run)');
}
```

## What the verification checks

| Check | Why |
| - | - |
| `tx.chainId` equals the intended network (8453 for Base) | Prevents signing on the wrong chain. |
| `tx.to` is the asset (for `approve`) or the vault (for `deposit`) | Payloads target protocol contracts directly; anything else is suspicious. |
| `tx.value` is absent or 0 for ERC-20 deposits | No native coin should move. |
| `approve(spender, amount)`: spender = vault, amount = your amount | Bounded approval, to the right spender. |
| `deposit(assets, receiver)`: assets = amount, receiver = user | The shares go to the user. |
| `amount ≤ asset.balanceNative` from the context | The API does not check the balance for you. |

The full checklist is on [transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety).

## Pitfalls

- **Human amounts.** `amount=1000` deposits 0.001 USDC. Multiply by `10^asset.decimals`; `amount=1.5` is a 400 ("Expected bigint").
- **Skipping the context.** It tells you whether the next step is `deposit` or something else (for example `request-deposit` on async vaults) and gives the asset address and decimals.
- **Wrong path order.** `/v2/transactions/deposit/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`; other orders return 400.
- **Missing `assetAddress`.** It is required.
- **Sending actions in parallel.** Wait for each receipt; the deposit reverts if the approval is not mined.
- **`simulate=true`.** Deprecated and ignored; v2 does not simulate. Simulate yourself (for example with `eth_call`) before signing.
- **Stale payloads.** Rebuild after a long delay or a failed action; re-read the context.
- **Appending the attribution suffix again.** Transactions API payloads already include it; see [TVL attribution suffix](/recipes/tvl-attribution-suffix).


# Recipe: withdraw from instant and queued vaults (redeem, request-redeem, claim-redeem)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/redeem-and-queued-withdrawal

> Executed recipe: read currentRedeemStep from the transaction context, build redeem with all=true for instant vaults or request-redeem then claim-redeem for queued vaults, track pendingRequests, and sign in order with viem (shown, not executed).

This recipe answers "how do I withdraw a user's position, including from vaults with a withdrawal queue?" It reads the transaction context to learn which redeem step comes next, builds the right payload, and shows how to sign it. Instant vaults need one `redeem`; queued vaults need `request-redeem`, a waiting period, then `claim-redeem`. Use it in any withdraw flow.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Amounts are base-unit integer strings. Original live outputs were recorded on 2026-10-23 against the public address `0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045`; outputs are real. Unit/sender edits were checked offline on 2026-10-30 (the unit check uses synthetic distinct asset/share balances). **No transaction was signed or sent.**

## Credit cost

Context 3 + payload 5 = **8 credits per step**. A queued withdrawal has two steps (request, later claim) plus polling the context (3 credits per poll) ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## Redeem steps

| `currentRedeemStep` | Meaning | Next call |
| - | - | - |
| `redeem` | Instant vault | `GET /v2/transactions/redeem/...` with `all=true` or an `amount` |
| `request-redeem` | Queued vault, nothing requested yet | `GET /v2/transactions/request-redeem/...` with `all=true` (full position; observed accepted, 200) or an `amount`, plus `assetAddress` |
| `claim-redeem` | A request is ready to claim | `GET /v2/transactions/claim-redeem/...` |

`redeemSteps[]` lists the full sequence for the vault; `pendingRequests.redeems[]` lists open requests with `status` (`pending` or `ready`) and `estimatedResolution`. Other steps exist on some vaults (for example `start-redeem-cooldown`); handle them explicitly rather than guessing.

## Partial withdrawals: convert assets to shares

`redeem` / `request-redeem` take **share base units** for ERC-4626, ERC-7540, Ethena, Veda/BoringVault and Compound v2 (cTokens). Aave v3/v4, Compound v3 and borrow-market aliases take **underlying-asset base units** instead. Lido requests take **stETH vault-token base units**, not an assumed exact ETH conversion. For a full exit, prefer `all=true`.

For a share-unit protocol, `shares = assets / sharePrice`; submit `amount = floor((assetBaseUnits / 10^asset.decimals) / sharePrice * 10^lpToken.decimals)`. Get `sharePrice` (asset tokens per share, already decimals-adjusted) from `GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}` or the detailed-vault record; read `asset.decimals` and `lpToken.decimals` from the detailed vault/context. Use decimal or integer-rational arithmetic, never JavaScript `Number` for base-unit integers. Worked preview using the cached Base Steakhouse price `1.01395919150542`, 6 asset decimals and 18 share decimals: 100 USDC is `100000000` asset base units; `floor(100 / 1.01395919150542 * 10^18) = 98623298489489023703` share base units. Pass that integer as the redeem `amount`, **not** `100000000`.

This is a rounded-down estimate, not a guarantee of exactly 100 USDC: indexed/NRT prices have finite precision and can move. For an exact asset-target exit, use the vault's on-chain `previewWithdraw` / conversion method and verify rounding, share balance and decoded calldata before signing; never silently cap the requested exit to available holdings.

## curl

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/redeem-and-queued-withdrawal.md

Lido stETH is a queued vault: `request-redeem` (approve + request) now, `claim-redeem` once the request is ready.

## TypeScript

```typescript
// Withdraw from instant and queued (request -> wait -> claim) vaults. Read-only: builds payloads only.
const API = 'https://api.vaults.fyi';
const headers = { 'x-api-key': process.env.VAULTSFYI_API_KEY! };
const USER = '0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045';

async function get(path: string, params: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const qs = new URLSearchParams(params);
  const res = await fetch(`${API}${path}${qs.size ? `?${qs}` : ''}`, { headers });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
  return res.json();
}

async function planWithdrawal(network: string, vaultId: string) {
  const ctx = await get(`/v2/transactions/context/${USER}/${network}/${vaultId}`);
  const step: string = ctx.currentRedeemStep; // redeem | request-redeem | claim-redeem | ...
  const { address: assetAddress, positionValueInAsset } = ctx.asset;
  console.log(`${network}/${vaultId}: steps ${ctx.redeemSteps.map((s: any) => s.name).join(' -> ')}, next = ${step}`);

  let query: Record<string, string>;
  if (step === 'redeem') query = { assetAddress, all: 'true' }; // instant: full position
  // This example is Lido: request stETH vault-token base units, not ETH asset units.
  else if (step === 'request-redeem') query = { assetAddress, amount: ctx.lpToken.balanceNative };
  else if (step === 'claim-redeem') query = { assetAddress };
  else { console.log(`  step ${step}: handle explicitly`); return; }

  const p = await get(`/v2/transactions/${step}/${USER}/${network}/${vaultId}`, query);
  for (const a of p.actions) console.log(`  build ${step}: ${a.name}  to=${a.tx.to}  chainId=${a.tx.chainId}`);

  const pending = ctx.pendingRequests?.redeems ?? []; // key absent when nothing is queued
  for (const r of pending) console.log(`  pending: status=${r.status} estimatedResolution=${r.estimatedResolution}`);
  if (!pending.length) console.log('  no pending redeem requests');
}

await planWithdrawal('base', '0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845'); // instant (ERC-4626)
await planWithdrawal('mainnet', '0xae7ab96520DE3A18E5e111B5EaAb095312D7fE84'); // queued (Lido stETH)
```

The test wallet has no position in the Base vault (position 0), so the redeem payload is valid but would redeem nothing; a real UI should skip it.

## Signing with viem (not executed)

Same pattern for every redeem step: verify chain and target, then send `actions[currentActionIndex:]` in order, waiting for each receipt. The branch runs only with `SEND=1`.

```typescript
// Sign and send a redeem payload with viem, IN ORDER, only when SEND=1. Tests never set SEND.
import { createPublicClient, createWalletClient, getAddress, http, type Hex } from 'viem';
import { privateKeyToAccount } from 'viem/accounts';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';

const API = 'https://api.vaults.fyi';
const headers = { 'x-api-key': process.env.VAULTSFYI_API_KEY! };
const USER = '0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045';
const VAULT_ID = '0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845'; // instant ERC-4626 vault on Base
const USDC = '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913';

const qs = new URLSearchParams({ assetAddress: USDC, all: 'true' }); // all=true: the whole position
const res = await fetch(`${API}/v2/transactions/redeem/${USER}/base/${VAULT_ID}?${qs}`, { headers });
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
const payload = await res.json();

type Action = { name: string; tx: { to: Hex; chainId: number; data?: Hex; value?: string } };
const actions: Action[] = payload.actions.slice(payload.currentActionIndex);
for (const a of actions) { // verify before anything is signed
  if (a.tx.chainId !== base.id) throw new Error(`wrong chain ${a.tx.chainId}`);
  if (getAddress(a.tx.to) !== getAddress(VAULT_ID)) throw new Error(`unexpected target ${a.tx.to}`);
  console.log(`verified: ${a.name}`);
}

if (process.env.SEND === '1') {
  const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PRIVATE_KEY as Hex); // USER's key; never hard-code it
  const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: base, transport: http() });
  const pub = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
  for (const a of actions) {
    const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({ to: a.tx.to, ...(a.tx.data !== undefined ? { data: a.tx.data } : {}), value: BigInt(a.tx.value ?? 0) });
    const receipt = await pub.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash }); // wait before the next action
    if (receipt.status !== 'success') throw new Error(`${a.name} reverted: ${hash}`);
  }
} else {
  console.log('SEND!=1: not signing (dry run)');
}
```

## Pitfalls

- **Calling `redeem` on a queued vault.** Read `currentRedeemStep` first; a single `redeem` is not enough for queued vaults.
- **Claiming too early.** Build `claim-redeem` only when the context says `currentRedeemStep: "claim-redeem"` and the request's `status` is `ready`.
- **`all=true` beyond `redeem`.** The spec documents it for `redeem`, but live it is also accepted on `request-redeem` and `claim-redeem` (observed 2026-10-23, 200 on a Lagoon queued vault). `assetAddress` is still required: `all=true` without it returns 400 `assetAddress Required`. For a full queued withdrawal, prefer `request-redeem` with `all=true` over computing an amount: on `redeem` and `request-redeem` it replaces `amount` and redeems the wallet's full share balance. On `claim-redeem` it is accepted and ignored.
- **The amount unit for `request-redeem` and partial `redeem` depends on the protocol.** `amount` is passed to the vault contract unchanged: on most vaults (ERC-4626, ERC-7540, Ethena, Veda, Compound v2) it is in **vault-share base units** (`lpToken.decimals`); on asset-based lending markets such as Aave and Compound v3 it is in underlying-asset base units. Observed on 2026-10-23 on one ERC-4626 vault (Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition on Base): `redeem` with `amount=1000000` produced calldata `redeem(0x0f4240, receiver, owner)`, i.e. shares, not USDC. Prefer `all=true` for full withdrawals; for partial ones, decode the calldata. The Lido example uses `lpToken.balanceNative` (stETH vault-token units); do not reuse an underlying-asset position amount for a share-unit protocol.
- **`pendingRequests` may be `null`** (as above) or omit `redeems`. Treat both as "no requests".
- **Timestamps in `pendingRequests`** (`estimatedResolution`, `requestTimestamp`) are Unix seconds. `pendingRequests` is filled only for some queue protocols; the signal every vault provides is `currentRedeemStep` becoming `claim-redeem`.


# Recipe: claim every pending reward for a wallet
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/claim-rewards

> Executed recipe: read GET /v2/transactions/rewards/context/{userAddress} (claimable is an object keyed by network), pass the claimIds as repeated keys to GET /v2/transactions/rewards/claim/{userAddress}, verify, and sign per network with viem (shown, not executed).

This recipe answers "how do I claim every pending reward for this wallet, on every network?" It reads the wallet's claimable rewards, builds the claim transactions per network, verifies them, and shows how to sign them. Use it for "claim all" buttons and reward-harvesting agents. The claimable rewards observed in testing were Merkl rewards.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23 against the public address `0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045`; outputs are real. **No transaction was signed or sent.**

## Credit cost

| Call | Cost |
| - | - |
| `GET /v2/transactions/rewards/context/{userAddress}` | 3 |
| `GET /v2/transactions/rewards/claim/{userAddress}` (one per network in these examples) | 5 |

One network with rewards: **8 credits** ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## Response shapes

- `rewards/context` → `{ claimable: { <network>: [ { claimId, asset: { symbol, claimableAmountInUsd?, ... } } ] }, actionUrl }`. `claimable` is an **object keyed by network name**, not an array.
- `rewards/claim?claimIds=…&claimIds=…` → `{ <network>: { currentActionIndex, actions: [ { name, tx: { to, chainId, data, value? } } ] } }`, also keyed by network.
- `claimIds` is a required array parameter: **repeat the key** once per id. Real ids look like `merkl:mainnet:0x3Ef3…-0xb755…`.

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/claim-rewards.md

## Signing with viem (not executed)

```typescript
// Sign and send reward claims with viem, one network at a time, IN ORDER, only when SEND=1.
import { createPublicClient, createWalletClient, http, type Chain, type Hex } from 'viem';
import { privateKeyToAccount } from 'viem/accounts';
import { arbitrum, base, mainnet, optimism } from 'viem/chains';

const API = 'https://api.vaults.fyi';
const headers = { 'x-api-key': process.env.VAULTSFYI_API_KEY! };
const USER = '0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045';
const CHAINS: Record<string, Chain> = { mainnet, base, arbitrum, optimism }; // API network name -> viem chain

const get = async (path: string) => {
  const r = await fetch(`${API}${path}`, { headers });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}: ${await r.text()}`);
  return r.json();
};

const { claimable } = await get(`/v2/transactions/rewards/context/${USER}`); // keyed by network
for (const [network, claims] of Object.entries<{ claimId: string }[]>(claimable)) {
  const chain = CHAINS[network];
  if (!chain) { console.log(`skip ${network}: add its viem chain`); continue; }
  const qs = new URLSearchParams(claims.map((c): [string, string] => ['claimIds', c.claimId]));
  const plan = (await get(`/v2/transactions/rewards/claim/${USER}?${qs}`))[network];
  const actions: { name: string; tx: { to: Hex; chainId: number; data?: Hex; value?: string } }[] =
    plan.actions.slice(plan.currentActionIndex);
  for (const a of actions) {
    if (a.tx.chainId !== chain.id) throw new Error(`${a.name}: chainId ${a.tx.chainId} != ${chain.id}`);
    if (BigInt(a.tx.value ?? 0) !== 0n) throw new Error(`${a.name}: claims should not send native value`);
    console.log(`verified ${network}: ${a.name} -> ${a.tx.to}`);
  }
  if (process.env.SEND !== '1') { console.log('SEND!=1: not signing (dry run)'); continue; }
  const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PRIVATE_KEY as Hex); // USER's key; never hard-code it
  const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain, transport: http() });
  const pub = createPublicClient({ chain, transport: http() });
  for (const a of actions) {
    const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({ to: a.tx.to, ...(a.tx.data !== undefined ? { data: a.tx.data } : {}), value: BigInt(a.tx.value ?? 0) });
    if ((await pub.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })).status !== 'success') throw new Error(`${a.name} reverted`);
  }
}
```

## Pitfalls

- **Iterating `claimable` as an array.** It is an object keyed by network.
- **Invented or stale claim ids.** Always take ids from a fresh context call.
- **Comma-joined `claimIds`.** Repeat the key.
- **POST.** Both endpoints are GET.
- **Per-vault vs wallet-level claims.** This recipe uses the wallet-level reward endpoints. Some vaults also expose a per-vault claim step via `/v2/transactions/{action}/...`; check the vault's transaction context.
- **Dust claims.** Compare `claimableAmountInUsd` with the expected gas cost before suggesting a claim.


# Recipe: near-real-time share price for a deposit preview
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/near-real-time-share-price

> Executed recipe: read sharePrice, totalAssets, totalSupply and underlyingAssetPrice from GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}, convert units with asset and lpToken decimals, and preview shares for a deposit, in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "what is the vault's share price right now?" The standard index refreshes about hourly; the near-real-time (NRT) endpoints read fresher on-chain state. The recipe reads all four NRT metrics, checks them against each other, and previews how many shares a 1,000 USDC deposit buys. Use it for deposit previews and fresh TVL figures.

Every request goes to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Original live outputs were recorded on 2026-10-23; the BigInt ratio update was replayed offline against cached responses on 2026-10-30, without API calls.

## Credit cost

Each of the five `/v2/nrt/vault/*` endpoints costs **1 credit** per call and needs an API key (no x402). The Python and TypeScript examples also call `GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}` (3 credits) for decimals and symbols; cache that, because decimals don't change.

## Endpoints and units

| Endpoint | Field | Unit |
| - | - | - |
| `GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}` | all four below | — |
| `…/sharePrice` | `sharePrice` | number: deposit asset per share, decimals already applied |
| `…/totalAssets` | `totalAssets` | string, **asset** base units (÷ 10^`asset.decimals`) |
| `…/totalSupply` | `totalSupply` | string, **share** base units (÷ 10^`lpToken.decimals`) |
| `…/underlyingAssetPrice` | `underlyingAssetPrice` | number, USD per asset token |

`asset.decimals` and `lpToken.decimals` can differ (USDC has 6, this vault's share token has 18).

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/near-real-time-share-price.md

## Python

```python
"""Fresh share price for a deposit preview, from the near-real-time (NRT) endpoint."""
import os
from decimal import Decimal

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}
NETWORK, VAULT_ID = "base", "0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845"

# Decimals come from the indexed vault record (asset.decimals and lpToken.decimals can differ).
vault = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/detailed-vaults/{NETWORK}/{VAULT_ID}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30).json()
nrt = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/nrt/vault/{NETWORK}/{VAULT_ID}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30).json()

share_price = Decimal(str(nrt["sharePrice"]))  # asset per share, decimals-adjusted (number)
total_assets = Decimal(nrt["totalAssets"]) / 10 ** vault["asset"]["decimals"]     # asset base units
total_supply = Decimal(nrt["totalSupply"]) / 10 ** vault["lpToken"]["decimals"]   # SHARE base units
print(f'sharePrice {share_price:.6f} {vault["asset"]["symbol"]}/share')
print(f"check: totalAssets/totalSupply = {total_assets / total_supply:.6f}")
print(f'underlying price ${nrt["underlyingAssetPrice"]}')

deposit = Decimal(1000)  # 1,000 USDC
print(f"preview: {deposit} {vault['asset']['symbol']} -> ~{deposit / share_price:,.4f} {vault['lpToken']['symbol']}")
```

## TypeScript

`totalAssets / totalSupply` (after each is scaled by its own decimals) equals `sharePrice`, which confirms the units.

## Pitfalls

- **Dividing `totalSupply` by the asset's decimals.** It is in share units; use `lpToken.decimals`.
- **Treating the preview as exact.** Deposits can incur fees or rounding; the on-chain `previewDeposit` is authoritative.
- **Polling NRT for lists.** NRT is per vault; use `/v2/detailed-vaults` for many vaults.
- **"Sub-second" claims.** NRT values are read from the chain's latest block on each call, with no response cache, so they are typically at most a block or a second old. The response time is a separate matter.


# Recipe: handle errors, soft errors and rate limits (402, 401, 400, 429)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/handle-errors-and-retries

> Executed recipe: a small client wrapper that branches on HTTP status, explains 402 without a key vs 401 invalid key vs 403 credits exhausted, parses 400 validation issues, surfaces 200 soft errors, reads x-ratelimit-* headers and retries only retryable statuses.

This recipe answers "why did my call fail, and should my client retry?" It shows what each failure looks like on the live API and gives a copy-paste wrapper in Python and TypeScript that branches on the HTTP status, retries only what is retryable, and turns soft errors into exceptions. Use it as the base client for any integration or agent.

Requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real and trimmed. The 429 and 403 branches were not triggered (the tests stay far below the limit and the key had credits).

## Credit cost

Each successful call costs its normal price ([credits](/plans/credits)). Requests without a key are not charged credits: they get a 402 payment challenge. Requests that don't return 200 (400, 404, 500 and so on) are not charged.

## Status codes at a glance

| Status | Meaning on vaults.fyi | Retry? |
| - | - | - |
| 200 + non-empty `errors.unsupported*` | A filter value was not recognised (for example a comma-joined array) | No, fix the filter |
| 400 | Validation error; `message` is a JSON-encoded list of issues | No |
| 401 | Key sent but invalid (message says "required") | No |
| 402 | **No `x-api-key` header** on a v2 endpoint: an x402 payment challenge | No: add the key, or pay via [x402](/ai-agents/x402) |
| 403 | Credits exhausted (spec; not observed) | No: top up |
| 404 | Unknown route | No |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded (spec; not observed) | Yes, after `retry-after` / `x-ratelimit-reset` |
| 500 | Server error | No (at most once) |
| 502, 503, 504 | Upstream unavailable or timeout | Yes, with backoff |

The full catalogue with bodies is on [errors](/api-reference/errors).

## What failures look like (curl)

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/handle-errors-and-retries.md

- The 402 body is an x402 v2 challenge. `accepts[0].amount` is the price in USDC base units: 8000 = $0.008 for this call.
- The comma-joined array returned **200** with zero results and the whole string in `errors.unsupportedNetworks`.
- Rate-limit headers on that key: 600 requests per 60-second window. They are absent on 401, 402 and route-404 responses.

## Python wrapper

```python
"""A vaults.fyi client wrapper: branch on HTTP status, retry only what is retryable, surface soft errors."""
import json
import os
import random
import time

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
RETRYABLE = {408, 429, 502, 503, 504}


class VaultsError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, body):
        self.status, self.body = status, body
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}: {body}")


def call(path, params=None, api_key=None, max_attempts=4):
    headers = {"x-api-key": api_key} if api_key else {}
    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
        r = requests.get(f"{API}{path}", params=params, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        if r.ok:
            body = r.json()
            bad = {k: v for k, v in (body.get("errors") or {}).items() if v} if isinstance(body, dict) else {}
            if bad:  # 200 + errors.unsupported*: a bad filter value, not "no results"
                raise VaultsError(200, {"softErrors": bad})
            remaining = r.headers.get("x-ratelimit-remaining")
            if remaining is not None and int(remaining) < 5:  # slow down before you hit 429
                time.sleep(int(r.headers.get("x-ratelimit-reset", "1")))
            return body
        try:
            body = r.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = r.text
        if r.status_code in RETRYABLE and attempt < max_attempts:
            wait = r.headers.get("retry-after") or r.headers.get("x-ratelimit-reset")
            delay = float(wait) if wait else min(30, 2 ** attempt) + random.random()
            time.sleep(delay)
            continue
        if r.status_code == 400 and isinstance(body, dict) and str(body.get("message", "")).startswith("["):
            body["issues"] = json.loads(body["message"])  # validation: JSON-encoded list of issues
        raise VaultsError(r.status_code, body)  # 400/401/402/403/404/500: fix the request, don't retry


KEY = os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]

# 402: no key. The body is an x402 challenge; accepts[0].amount is USDC base units (6 decimals).
try:
    call("/v2/detailed-vaults", {"perPage": 1})
except VaultsError as e:
    print(e.status, "->", "add x-api-key or pay via x402; price", e.body["accepts"][0]["amount"], "USDC base units")

# 401: key sent but invalid (the message says 'required'; branch on the status).
try:
    call("/v2/networks", api_key="not-a-real-key")
except VaultsError as e:
    print(e.status, "->", e.body.get("message", "")[:60])

# 400: validation error with a parseable issue list.
try:
    call("/v2/detailed-vaults", {"sortBy": "apy", "perPage": 1}, api_key=KEY)
except VaultsError as e:
    i = e.body["issues"][0]
    print(e.status, "->", i["path"], i["message"][:40], "options:", i.get("options"))

# 200 with soft errors: a comma-joined array is treated as ONE unknown network.
try:
    call("/v2/detailed-vaults", {"allowedNetworks": "base,arbitrum", "perPage": 1}, api_key=KEY)
except VaultsError as e:
    print(e.status, "->", e.body)

# Success path.
nets = call("/v2/networks", api_key=KEY)
print("200 ->", len(nets), "networks")
```

## SDK behaviour

The SDKs handle errors differently from these wrappers. Tested against a local stub server (no API calls):

| Status | `vaultsfyi` 1.3.0 (Python), `max_retries=3` | `@vaultsfyi/sdk` 2.3.14 (TypeScript) |
| - | - | - |
| 400, 402, 404 | `HttpResponseError` (`status_code` set), 1 request | `Error` subclass with only `message`, 1 request |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError`, 1 request | same plain error, no status |
| 403 | `ForbiddenError`, 1 request | same plain error, no status |
| 429, 500, 503 | `NetworkError` after 4 requests (3 retries, about 6 s) | plain error after 1 request (no retries) |

So in Python, catch `NetworkError` for exhausted 429/5xx retries (not `RateLimitError`), and in TypeScript wrap SDK calls with your own retry. See [SDK reference: errors](/sdk/reference#errors-and-retries).

## Pitfalls

- **Reading 402 as "bad key".** 402 means **no** key reached the API. Check the header name is exactly `x-api-key` (REST). `Authorization: Bearer` is only for the [MCP server](/ai-agents/mcp-server).
- **Retrying 401/402/403/400.** They won't succeed on retry.
- **Treating 200 as success.** Check `errors.unsupportedNetworks`, `unsupportedAssets` and `unsupportedProtocols`.
- **Parsing `statusCode` from the body.** Not every error has it; branch on the HTTP status.
- **Inventing a `Retry-After` guarantee.** It was not observed on 429; fall back to `x-ratelimit-reset`, then exponential backoff with jitter.
- **Retrying signing or broadcasting.** Retry read-only GETs only. See [transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety).


# Recipe: estimate the credit cost of a workload (hourly dashboard example)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/estimate-credit-cost

> Executed recipe: compute vaults.fyi credits from the published base and per-item costs, price a real call from itemsOnPage, and size an hourly 200-vault dashboard (601 credits per refresh, 432,720 per month, Growth plan).

This recipe answers "how many credits will my integration use per month, and which plan fits?" It prices one real call from its `itemsOnPage`, then models a monthly schedule from the published credit table. Use it before you build a polling loop or let an agent call the API on a timer.

Requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Costs come from the [credits](/plans/credits) table; the API does not return a per-request credit count. Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23.

## The formula

**credits = base cost per call + (cost per item × items returned)**

| Endpoint | Base | Per item |
| - | -: | - |
| `GET /v2/vaults` | 1 | — |
| `GET /v2/detailed-vaults` | 1 | 3 per vault |
| `GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}` | 3 | — |
| `GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/apy` | 1 | 1 per point |
| `GET /v2/benchmarks/{network}` | 3 | — |
| `GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}` | 5 | — |
| `GET /v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options/{userAddress}` | 1 | 2 per vault |
| `GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | 3 | — |
| `GET /v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | 5 | — |

The NRT endpoints (`/v2/nrt/vault/*`) cost 1 credit per call. `/v2/health` is free. Requests that don't return 200 are not charged.

## Python

```python
"""Estimate credits before you build: price one real call, then a monthly schedule. No API key spent
beyond the single sample call. Costs are from the published credits table (/plans/credits)."""
import math
import os

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}

# (base CU per call, CU per datapoint) -- docs table, not returned by the API.
COST = {
    "/v2/vaults": (1, 0),
    "/v2/detailed-vaults": (1, 3),
    "/v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}": (3, 0),
    "/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/apy": (1, 1),
    "/v2/benchmarks/{network}": (3, 0),
    "/v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}": (5, 0),
    "/v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options/{userAddress}": (1, 2),
    "/v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}": (3, 0),
    "/v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}": (5, 0),
}


def credits(endpoint, datapoints=0, calls=1):
    base, per = COST[endpoint]
    return calls * base + per * datapoints


# 1) Price a real call: itemsOnPage is the datapoint count for list endpoints.
r = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/detailed-vaults", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30,
                 params=[("allowedNetworks", "base"), ("allowedAssets", "USDC"), ("perPage", 3)])
r.raise_for_status()
n = r.json()["itemsOnPage"]
print(f"this call returned {n} vaults -> {credits('/v2/detailed-vaults', n)} credits")

# 2) Hourly dashboard: 200 vaults of detailed data, 24 x 30 refreshes a month.
per_refresh = credits("/v2/detailed-vaults", 200)          # one call with perPage=200 -> 601
monthly = per_refresh * 24 * 30
print(f"hourly 200-vault refresh: {per_refresh} CU/refresh, {monthly:,} CU/month, "
      f"${monthly * 0.002:,.2f} at pay-as-you-go $0.002/credit")

# Splitting into pages adds 1 CU per extra call: 4 pages of 50 = 4 + 600 = 604.
print("same data in 4 pages of 50:", credits("/v2/detailed-vaults", 200, calls=4), "CU")

# 3) 90 days of daily APY for 10 vaults (1 call each; a 90-day window returned 90 points).
print("90-day daily history x 10 vaults:", 10 * credits("/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/apy", 90), "CU")

# 4) One full deposit flow: context + payload.
flow = credits("/v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}") + credits(
    "/v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}")
print("one deposit flow (context + payload):", flow, "CU")

PLANS = [("Analyst", 250_000), ("Growth", 500_000), ("Builder", 1_000_000)]  # credits/month, /plans/overview
fits = next((name for name, cap in PLANS if cap >= monthly), "Enterprise")
print(f"smallest plan that covers {monthly:,} CU/month: {fits}")
```

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/estimate-credit-cost.md

## The dashboard answer

- One refresh of 200 vaults with `perPage=200`: 1 + 3 × 200 = **601 credits**.
- Hourly for a 30-day month: 601 × 24 × 30 = **432,720 credits**.
- Plans: Analyst includes 250,000 (too small); **Growth** includes 500,000 and fits; Builder includes 1,000,000. Pay-as-you-go would cost $865.44. Plan prices are on [plans](/plans/overview).
- Splitting into pages adds 1 credit per extra call (4 pages of 50 = 604).
- When the key's credit balance reaches zero, priced endpoints return 403 until you top up or upgrade; see [credits](/plans/credits#when-credits-run-out). Pay-as-you-go keys have no spending cap: usage is billed per credit with no upper limit, so set your own budget alerts or call limits if you need one.

## Pitfalls

- **Forgetting the base cost.** 200 vaults cost 601, not 600.
- **Using v1 costs** (4 per vault). v2 detailed vaults cost 3 per vault.
- **Mixing x402 prices and credits.** x402 prices are dollars per request; on 2026-10-23 they matched credits × $0.002, but this is not documented as a rule.
- **Over-polling.** Indexed data refreshes about hourly; polling more often mostly re-buys the same data.
- **Large historical windows at `granularity=1hour`.** 30 days hourly on the combined endpoint is 2,163 credits; use `1day` and the single-series endpoints.


# Recipe: map network names and chain IDs, and find a vaultId
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/network-and-vault-ids

> Executed recipe: resolve user input such as "Ethereum" or "chain 8453" to API network values (mainnet, base or CAIP-2) with GET /v2/networks, and get vaultId values from list endpoints, including non-address vaultIds.

This recipe answers "what do I put in `{network}` and `{vaultId}`?" It maps everyday names and chain IDs to the values the API accepts, and shows where `vaultId` comes from, including the vaults whose `vaultId` is not a plain contract address. Use it in any code or agent that turns user words into API paths.

Requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real.

## Credit cost

`GET /v2/networks` 1 credit, `GET /v2/vaults` 1 credit per call (3,662 vaults in one call with `perPage=5000`). **2 credits** total; cache both ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## The rules

| Input | API value | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| "Ethereum", "eth" | `mainnet` or `eip155:1` | `ethereum` is rejected |
| "chain 8453", `8453` | `base` or `eip155:8453` | Bare chain IDs are rejected; map them via `/v2/networks` |
| `eip155:42161` | `arbitrum` or `eip155:42161` | CAIP-2 is accepted as is |
| Solana | not a v2 network | Use the Beta `/beta/svm/*` endpoints, which have no network segment ([Solana deposit](/recipes/solana-deposit)) |

`GET /v2/networks` returns a plain array of `{ name, chainId, networkCaip }` (22 networks on 2026-10-23).

**`vaultId`** is the stable vault identifier used in every `{vaultId}` path segment. It is usually the vault contract address, but not always: on 2026-10-23, 53 of 3,662 vaults had a non-address `vaultId` (for example Aave v4 spokes such as `0x94e7…c485-0`). Always take `vaultId` from `data[].vaultId` of `/v2/vaults` or `/v2/detailed-vaults`; don't derive it from `address`.

## Python

```python
"""Resolve user words ("Ethereum", "chain 8453") to API network ids, and find vaultIds (incl. non-address ids)."""
import os
import re

import requests

API = "https://api.vaults.fyi"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"]}

networks = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/networks", headers=HEADERS, timeout=30).json()  # plain array
by_chain = {n["chainId"]: n for n in networks}
ALIASES = {"ethereum": "mainnet", "eth": "mainnet"}  # 'ethereum' is NOT a valid network value


def to_network(user_input):
    s = str(user_input).strip().lower().removeprefix("chain ")
    if s.isdigit():
        return by_chain[int(s)]["name"]  # bare chain ids are rejected by the API -> map them
    s = ALIASES.get(s, s)
    for n in networks:
        if s in (n["name"], n["networkCaip"]):
            return n["name"]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown network {user_input!r}")


for q in ["Ethereum", "chain 8453", "eip155:42161", "optimism"]:
    name = to_network(q)
    caip = next(n["networkCaip"] for n in networks if n["name"] == name)
    print(f"{q!r:16} -> {name} (or {caip})")

# vaultId: take it from list endpoints. Most are addresses; some (e.g. Aave v4 spokes) are not.
vaults = requests.get(f"{API}/v2/vaults", headers=HEADERS, params={"perPage": 5000}, timeout=60).json()["data"]
non_addr = [v for v in vaults if not re.fullmatch(r"0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", v["vaultId"])]
print(f"{len(vaults)} vaults, {len(non_addr)} with a non-address vaultId, e.g.:")
for v in non_addr[:2]:
    print(f'  {v["network"]["name"]} {v["name"]}: vaultId={v["vaultId"]} address={v["address"]}')
```

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/network-and-vault-ids.md

## Pitfalls

- **`network=ethereum`, `network=1`, `network=8453`.** All rejected; use `mainnet`, `base` or CAIP-2.
- **Assuming `vaultId == address`.** True for most vaults, false for some. Use the `vaultId` field.
- **SDK naming.** The Python SDK calls this argument `vault_address`, but you must pass the `vaultId`. The TypeScript SDK uses `path.vaultId`. See [SDK reference](/sdk/reference).
- **Solana addresses in v2 paths.** Solana vaults live under `/beta/svm/*` with base58 `vaultAddress`.


# Recipe: TVL attribution suffix for calldata you build yourself
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/tvl-attribution-suffix

> Executed recipe: get the attribution suffix from GET /v2/transactions/suffix/{userAddress}/{vaultId} (hex without 0x) and append it to self-encoded calldata; Transactions API payloads already include it.

This recipe answers "I build vault transactions myself; how do I get the deposits attributed to my app?" It fetches the attribution suffix and appends it to calldata you encode yourself. If you use the Transactions API payloads, **do nothing**: they already include it. Use it in apps with their own transaction builder.

Requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real. Nothing was signed.

## Credit cost

The suffix endpoint costs **1 credit** ([credits](/plans/credits)); earlier docs called it free. It needs an API key with attribution enabled (otherwise 400, not charged). The suffix is deterministic for your API key, the user and the vault, so cache it.

## The endpoint

`GET /v2/transactions/suffix/{userAddress}/{vaultId}` returns `{ "suffix": "<hex>" }`. The hex has **no `0x` prefix**. There is **no network segment** in this path.

curl / Python / TypeScript versions of this recipe's code: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/tvl-attribution-suffix.md

## TypeScript (viem)

```typescript
// Append the vaults.fyi attribution suffix to calldata you encode yourself.
import { encodeFunctionData, erc4626Abi, type Hex } from 'viem';

const API = 'https://api.vaults.fyi';
const headers = { 'x-api-key': process.env.VAULTSFYI_API_KEY! };
const USER = '0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045';
const VAULT_ID = '0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845'; // no network segment in this path

const res = await fetch(`${API}/v2/transactions/suffix/${USER}/${VAULT_ID}`, { headers });
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
const { suffix } = (await res.json()) as { suffix: string }; // hex WITHOUT 0x

const calldata = encodeFunctionData({ abi: erc4626Abi, functionName: 'deposit', args: [25_000_000n, USER] });
const withSuffix = (calldata + suffix) as Hex; // plain concatenation: never insert a second 0x
console.log('suffix', suffix, `(${suffix.length / 2} bytes, starts with 0x? ${suffix.startsWith('0x')})`);
console.log('calldata', calldata.length, 'chars ->', withSuffix.length, 'chars; ends with suffix:', withSuffix.endsWith(suffix));
```

The suffix adds 24 bytes after the ABI-encoded arguments; contracts ignore trailing calldata, and vaults.fyi reads it to attribute the deposit.

## Pitfalls

- **Adding `0x` again.** Concatenate the raw hex.
- **Appending to Transactions API payloads.** They already carry it; a double suffix is wasted gas and may break attribution.
- **Adding a network segment.** The path is `/suffix/{userAddress}/{vaultId}` only.
- **Using it with smart-wallet batching.** Keep the suffix on the inner vault call (pass each vault call's `data` through unchanged) and generate it for the address the vault sees as the depositor: for a smart wallet, the smart-account address, not the signer.


# Recipe: Solana (SVM) vault deposit payload (Beta)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/recipes/solana-deposit

> Executed recipe: build an unsigned Solana deposit with the Beta /beta/svm/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{vaultAddress} endpoints (no network segment, base58 addresses, SPL mint as assetAddress, base-unit amount) and decode the base64 transaction, in curl, Python and TypeScript.

This recipe answers "how do I deposit into a Solana vault?" Solana is not a v2 network: it has its own **Beta** endpoints under `/beta/svm/*`, with base58 addresses and no network path segment. The recipe reads the context, builds an unsigned deposit for 1 USDC, and decodes the returned base64 transaction for signing. Use it to add Solana vaults next to EVM ones. Beta endpoints may change; monitor them ([versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).

Requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Beta endpoints need an API key. All code on this page was run on 2026-10-23; outputs are real. Nothing was signed.

## Credit cost

Context 3 + payload 5 = **8 credits** ([credits](/plans/credits)).

## EVM vs SVM paths

| | EVM (v2) | Solana (Beta) |
| - | - | - |
| Context | `/v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | `/beta/svm/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{vaultAddress}` |
| Payload | `/v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | `/beta/svm/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{vaultAddress}` |
| Actions | deposit, redeem, request-redeem, claim-redeem, … | deposit, redeem, request-redeem, confirm-redeem, complete-redeem |
| `tx` | `{ to, chainId, data, value? }` | `{ type: "solana", transaction: <base64> }` |
